title: PLAYABLE: 2nd Attempt at AI Game Dev Tool Pipeline
author: keithAtPlay
selftext:
**TLDR**: This game was made with [RUN.game](http://run.game/) (Claude + Cursor) in \~20 hours worth of prompting. Looking for genuine feedback on the output and whether it's worth investing more time to polish for production-level launch.

**Game Details:**

Title: ASCII Dungeon Master  
Desc: You are the dungeon. Adventurers are coming. Stop them.

**Playable Link**: [https://run.game/keithatplay/ascii-dungeon-master?gamename=ascii-dungeon-master](https://run.game/keithatplay/ascii-dungeon-master?gamename=ascii-dungeon-master)

**My Background** (bc it's relevant):  
I am a 25 year game dev / software engineering pro and have been working with pre-release AI models for the past 4+ years and loathe “vibe” anything. I will shout from my soapbox all day about how the models are ripe with issues and should only be used by experts that can tell when they’re wrong (bc they are wrong… *frequently*) and shouldn’t be trusted for more than a junior dev engineering expertise.

**Why Care**:  
With all that bullsh... I mean "background", I am very familiar with these models and their ability to code legit projects (as well as their weaknesses) and

This is my 2nd attempt at a completely hands-off game dev cycle using an end-to-end AI game dev.  I kept to ASCII part bc I wanted to make this game, but also so inconsistencies in image generation didn’t impact the output. (My first attempt was a 2+ years ago on FRVR's *earl*y platform.)

And, tbh, these guys are legit. They date back to old school flash web days and know what it means to be indie and build community.  They speak me.  Their tools are young, already pretty solid and all signs show they are listening to dev input. But, tools based on AI models are only as good as the AI models.

**Ask:**  
So, what do you think?? After 20+ hours, is this an appropriate prototype capable of being polished into a marketable build? Would **you** put $$ to market it with the expectation of a positive ROI?

**Project Specs**:  
Dev Cycle: 9 days (didn't start til day 2).  
AI Models:

* Claude & Cursor

Key dev points:

* Already had the concept prepped from previous design sessions
* ASCII by design, so fit my goals
* Total “Dev” Time: 20-25 hours 
   * <3-4 hours a day and some 0 days 
   * and a bit more at the end to push to submit

Key Dev Struggles (For the AI):

* Game states
   * Adding the demo mode on the start screen **exploded** regular gameplay when it should have been an easy isolated case with an auto-reload + random level assignment after 1000 turns.
* UI states
   * Related to game states, but kept breaking the flow or other functionality when a new UI popup or state was created.
* Replacing pre-existing functionality when clear pivots were made
   * For at least two of the growth rate calculations, it took serious prompting for the model to give up basing growth rates on turns and not upgrade levels.  Turn-based growth was a placeholder early on but I still feel is being used in several calculations.

**My assessment**:

Better than 2-3 years ago, but still required active prompting to achieve this.  It felt more like managing a team of interns with a few juniors who were supposed to be leading them.  I’m honestly afraid to even dig into the code for fear of wasting days trying to fix a flicker bug.  I might pass it to a few different models and get their analysis instead.

I stand by my position of: “AI Assistants are for Human Experts in their field to do more with the time they have”.
